text:
Jay Swidler of Vernon Township Republicans said IL 'education system should educate children, not indoctrinate'
Jay Swidler of Vernon Township GOP said Illinois schools should face scrutiny over classroom discussions involving gender identity, sexual orientation, and parental opt-out policies. Swidler made his statement to the Lake County Gazette on May 29.
"For years, many parents have felt ignored while schools embraced activist-driven lessons that belong at home, not in elementary classrooms," Swidler said. "Families should always have the ability to opt their children out of discussions they believe are age-inappropriate or politically charged. It is encouraging to finally see serious scrutiny directed at Illinois school systems that have resisted parental concerns. Our education system should educate children, not indoctrinate them."
Capitol News Illinois reported that as of April 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice was investigating 35 Illinois school districts and Chicago’s largest charter network over classroom discussions of sexual orientation and "gender ideology," parental opt-out policies, and transgender students’ access to bathrooms and sports teams. The inquiry cites Title IX and recent Supreme Court rulings involving parental rights.
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon said schools must allow parents to exempt children from instruction conflicting with family values, according to Capitol News Illinois.
The American College of Pediatricians said there is no long-term evidence supporting the safety or efficacy of puberty blockers, cross-sex hormones, or surgeries for transgender youth. The organization said parents need reliable data to provide informed consent and said such interventions can carry physical and mental health risks.
Jay Swidler is a resident of Buffalo Grove who was first elected chairman of the Vernon Township Republicans in 2024. The organization’s website says Swidler is focused on boosting Republican voter turnout, growing party membership, and communicating positions on issues important to Vernon Township voters.
